## Abstract

The paper considers the subject of critical phenomena in the physical world of thermodynamics and its analog in the economic world and the formation of bubbles in financial markets. Providing a review and comparison of a "bottom-up" approach based on statistical mechanics with a more "top-down" construction using iterative solutions to functional equations, both of which exhibit the required scale invariance (power laws) and fractal qualities seen near the critical points, and where the renormalization group theory provides a "bridge" between these two approaches both in a physical and mathematical sense.

*M840 Dissertation in Mathematics, The Open University.*

[Download the PDF](milne-2022-rg-functional-equations-critical-phenomena.pdf)

**Related:** [Fixed Points, Phase Transitions, and Diffusion Models](/posts/rg-diffusion-phase-transitions/) connects this dissertation's renormalization-group critical phenomena to the phase transitions found in hierarchical diffusion models.
